name: Glycogen Storage Disease Due to Glycogen Branching Enzyme Deficiency, Childhood Neuromuscular Form
aliases: Glycogen Storage Disease Type IV Childhood Neuromuscular Variant

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Glycogen Storage Disease Type IV Childhood Neuromuscular Form

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient glycogen branching enzyme activity in muscle or liver tissue
Progressive neuromuscular symptoms including hypotonia and muscle weakness presenting in early childhood
Identification of pathogenic variants in the GBE1 gene
Muscle biopsy showing abnormal glycogen with fewer branch points and polyglucosan bodies
Mild to moderate elevation of serum creatine kinase levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of deficient glycogen branching enzyme activity plus compatible clinical presentation and/or identification of pathogenic GBE1 variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle biopsy and genetic testing are critical for confirmation; clinical presentation alone is insufficient.

searchTerms: gradual weakness in upper legs and arms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypotonia with diminished deep tendon reflexes
searchTerms: low muscle tone with weak reflexes
floppy muscles and reduced tendon reflexes
hypotonia with diminished deep tendon reflexes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of polyglucosan bodies in muscle biopsy
searchTerms: polyglucosan bodies seen in muscle biopsy
abnormal glycogen deposits in muscle tissue

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to mild dyspnea
searchTerms: mild shortness of breath from weak breathing muscles
breathing difficulty due to respiratory muscle weakness
dyspnea caused by weak respiratory muscles

laboratory: Reduced glycogen branching enzyme activity in muscle or liver tissue
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle atrophy
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating polyglucosan bodies with PAS staining

distinguishingFeatures: Exercise intolerance with second wind phenomenon

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness in early childhood
Respiratory insufficiency due to diaphragmatic weakness
references: Burwinkel B, et al. Glycogen Storage Disease Type IV: Clinical and Molecular Aspects. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2017.
